sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/python_idioms.py
# ============================================================
# PYTHONIC IDIOMS & PERFORMANCE TRICKS
# ============================================================

# --- 1. Ternary expression ---
status = "adult" if age >= 18 else "minor"

# --- 2. Chained comparison ---
if 0 < x < 100:  # NOT: if x > 0 and x < 100
    pass

# --- 3. Multiple assignment ---
a, b, c = 1, 2, 3
first, *middle, last = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

# --- 4. Swap variables ---
a, b = b, a

# --- 5. Dictionary merge (3.9+) ---
merged = dict1 | dict2

# --- 6. String multiplication ---
separator = "-" * 50
matrix_row = [0] * 10

# --- 7. Truthiness ---
# Instead of: if len(my_list) > 0:
if my_list:   # Pythonic
    pass

# Instead of: if x == None:
if x is None:  # Pythonic (identity check)
    pass

# --- 8. EAFP over LBYL ---
# LBYL (Look Before You Leap) — C-style
if "key" in dictionary:
    value = dictionary["key"]

# EAFP (Easier to Ask Forgiveness than Permission) — Pythonic
try:
    value = dictionary["key"]
except KeyError:
    value = default

# Best: use .get()
value = dictionary.get("key", default)

# --- 9. Underscore conventions ---
_single_leading    = "internal use (convention)"
single_trailing_   = "avoid conflict with keyword (class_)"
__double_leading   = "name mangling"
__dunder__         = "magic/dunder methods"
_                  = "throwaway variable"

for _ in range(5):   # Don't need the loop variable
    pass

# --- 10. Conditional import ---
try:
    import ujson as json  # Fast JSON parser
except ImportError:
    import json           # Fallback to standard

# --- 11. Else clause on loops and try ---
# for/else: else runs if loop didn't break
for item in items:
    if condition(item):
        break
else:
    print("Not found!")

# try/else: else runs if no exception
try:
    result = operation()
except SomeError:
    handle_error()
else:
    process_result(result)  # Only if no exception

# --- 12. One-liner file read ---
content = open("file.txt").read()  # DON'T — file not properly closed
content = Path("file.txt").read_text()  # OK for small files

# --- 13. Flatten with sum (small lists only) ---
nested = [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]]
flat = sum(nested, [])  # [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] — O(n²), use chain for large

# --- 14. Dictionary as switch ---
def handle_action(action):
    handlers = {
        "start": lambda: "Starting...",
        "stop": lambda: "Stopping...",
        "restart": lambda: "Restarting...",
    }
    return handlers.get(action, lambda: "Unknown action")()

# --- 15. Walrus operator in real code ---
# Process chunks
while chunk := file.read(8192):
    process(chunk)

# Filter with computation
results = [y for x in data if (y := expensive(x)) > threshold]

# --- 16. Performance tips ---
# Use local variables (faster than global)
def fast_loop():
    local_func = len  # Cache built-in as local
    for item in big_list:
        local_func(item)

# Use dict/set for membership testing
# O(1) instead of O(n) for lists
good_set = set(big_list)
if item in good_set:  # Fast!
    pass

# Use generators for large data
total = sum(x * x for x in range(1_000_000))  # No list created

# String concatenation
parts = []
for item in items:
    parts.append(str(item))
result = "".join(parts)  # Much faster than += in loop
```
